entries.group: round v2.3 W1b destructive-authority discover survivor (ledger seq 13)
entries.grounds: discover L224-225 special-cases in-memory list[x].remove to kind='collection'. Round v2.3 re-measure of the W1b SCOPES widening (ledger seq 13): the same three survivors (L224 Eq->NotEq, L225 'collection' emptied, L224 'remove' emptied). The widened corpus (aisef2/, validation/v2, tests/v2, validation/v23, tests/v23) holds exactly ONE subscript-receiver .remove site — tests/v2/p0/test_arch_catalog.py:47, ledgered COLLECTION_METHOD — and each mutant can only MISCLASSIFY it from 'collection' to 'path', which check() flags as a target_kind mismatch: strictly fail-closed (a problem appears; none disappears). No fail-open, no live authority hole. The live-tree kill assertion (Checker.test_this_tree_passes_and_every_site_is_ledgered) is sealing-gated and skips in a mutant chain, so the misclassification goes unobserved there: a kill-set coverage gap (P2/v2.2.1), not an authority defect. Audited individually, not bulk-accepted (session 845c9f11, round v2.3).

entries.mutant: L470 string 'E5: the attempt could not be closed: ' emptied
entries.group: round v2.3 W1b E5 targeted campaign (9b30df44, 2026-11-22..25)
entries.grounds: story_runner.py:445/470 are the H5/H6 closure-fault notes: `e.add_note('E5: the attempt could not be closed: ...')` on an exception that is already propagating. The matrix proves the behavior that matters — the original exception object, its type, `raise ... from None`, and that closure faults write nothing more (F6, F13, F14, F22) — and no test pins the note's prose. The mutants change diagnostic wording only; propagation, masking rules and journal writes are unchanged.
consumers_checked: aisef2/orchestrate/story_runner.py:444-446 H6: add_note then `raise e from None` — the raise is what tests assert
aisef2/orchestrate/story_runner.py:468-471 same shape on the DECIDE..END closure try
exceptions_checked: tests/v2/test_v23_story_lifecycle.py F6/F13/F14/F22: assert the original type escapes unmasked and nothing more is written; note text unasserted by design

entries.group: round v2.3 W1b E5 targeted campaign (9b30df44, 2026-11-22..25)
entries.grounds: story_runner.py:418 is the H4 handler's stage-label fallback: `stage = st.at.name if st.at is not None else Stage.ACQUIRE.name`. The mutant changes only the LABEL used in the synthetic PROVIDER_RESULT closer detail and the failure detail when a fault precedes the FIRST advance (st.at is None). Containment, classify(UNKNOWN), the gate row (the `else` branch's constant 'resources') and propagation are unchanged and matrix-proven (F1-F25). The frozen fault matrix has no row injecting a fault before the first advance, so the label in that corner is unobserved: a named coverage gap of the frozen matrix (candidate tightening row for W2, owner's call), not an authority or classification defect. The wrong label cannot flip any decision: failure is already classify(UNKNOWN) and the row label does not come from this expression.

aisef2/orchestrate/story_runner.py:426-427 failure/detail: classify(FailureCode.UNKNOWN) independent of the label
